prompt_text: What is the best health insurance broker in Kansas City MO for someone who is self-employed?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t one single “best” broker for every self‑employed person — the right broker depends on your priorities (lowest premium, specific doctors/PO, HSA eligibility, willingness to manage QSEHRA or small‑group options, etc.). Instead of naming one definitive firm, here’s a practical way to get the best match plus a few reputable places to start.

How to pick the best broker for you
- Look for an independent agent/broker who can show plans from multiple carriers (not captive to one insurer).  
- Experience with ACA Marketplace/Missouri plans, and with self‑employed issues (income-based premium tax credits, APTC reconciliation, QSEHRA / HRA setup).  
- Licensed in Missouri and ideally in both MO and KS if you sometimes cross state lines for care.  
- Transparent about compensation (most individual plan brokers are paid by insurers, not you — but confirm).  
- Good references/reviews and willingness to explain tradeoffs (network, formularies, deductibles, HSA eligibility).  
- Willing to help with enrollment and year‑end income adjustments for advance premium tax credits.

Practical places to find reputable brokers/agents in Kansas City, MO
- HealthCare.gov agent/broker locator — finds brokers certified to enroll people in Marketplace plans (Missouri uses the federal exchange).  
- National online brokers that serve individuals: eHealth, HealthSherpa, GetInsured — good for quick comparisons and Marketplace-eligible enrollment help.  
- National/local associations: National Association of Health Underwriters (NAHU) “Find an Agent” tool to locate credentialed brokers.  
- Missouri Department of Commerce & Insurance — for verifying license status and any complaints.

Questions to ask a broker before you hire them
- Do you work with multiple carriers? Which ones here in Missouri?  
- Do you have experience helping self‑employed clients claim premium tax credits and reconcile APTC?  
- How do you get paid? Will I owe you anything?  
- Can you show plans that include my doctors/pharmacy?  
- Will you help me annually at open enrollment or if my income changes mid‑year?

If you want, I can:
- Look up and list 3–5 licensed independent brokers/agents in Kansas City, MO (I’ll need your ZIP code or neighborhood and whether you prefer in‑person or remote help), or  
- Compare 2–3 plan options (give me age, ZIP, household income, tobacco use, and any must‑have doctors or plan features).

Which would you like me to do next?
